Plain-English Causal Interpretation & Audit for a TMLE Fit

Source: R/tidymodels_verbs.R
explain_tmle.Rd

Translates a "tmle_fit" object into plain-English causal sentences, explains how strongly the TMLE targeting step corrected residual bias from the initial machine-learning fit, and runs a traffic-light diagnostic audit with actionable next steps (retarget(), autoplot(), augment()). summary(fit) delegates directly to explain_tmle().

Usage

explain_tmle(x, conf.level = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'tmle_fit'
summary(object, conf.level = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x, object

A fitted "tmle_fit" object.

conf.level

Confidence level for interval statements; defaults to the level stored on x (0.95 initially).

...

Currently unused.

Value

Invisibly returns a list with elements estimates (tibble) and health (1-row glance() tibble).

Examples

df <- sim_causal_cohort(n = 150, outcome_type = "binary", seed = 42)
fit <- tmle_spec(y, a, c(age, sex, lab_1, lab_2), estimand = c("ate", "rr")) |>
  set_resamples(v_folds = 3L) |>
  fit(df)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> ── Plain-English TMLE Summary ──
#> 
#> Cohort: 150 rows (150 with observed outcomes) | 3-fold cross-fitted
#> TMLE
#> 
#> ── 1. What the Causal Estimates Mean 
#> ℹ ATE (across the full study population): Treatment increases the expected outcome by 0.2381 units (95% CI [0.0808, 0.3954], p = 0.0030).
#> ℹ RR: Treatment corresponds to a 1.95x risk ratio (95.1% higher risk; 95% CI [1.25, 3.06], p = 0.0035).
#> 
#> ── 2. What the Targeting Step Did ("Predict, Then Target") 
#> Targeting nudged the initial ML plug-in predictions by +0.0449
#> (epsilon = 0.1295) to zero out residual confounding bias.
#> 
#> ── 3. Can I Trust These Numbers? (Health Check & Next Steps) 
#> ✔ Convergence: Bias-removal score equation solved (mean EIF = 7.14e-17).
#> ✔ Comparison overlap: 0.0% clipped at [0.081, 0.919] (effective n: 53.5 treated, 85 control).
#> ✔ Confounder balance: Max standardized difference fell from 0.465 to 0.064 (well below 0.10).
#> ! High leverage: Top observation accounts for 10.9% of variance. Inspect `augment(fit) |> dplyr::slice_max(.eif_leverage, n = 5)`.
#> Next steps: report_tmle(fit) for paper-ready prose | autoplot(fit,
#> type = 'dashboard') for visual audit.
